meta.description: Credited to Mary Kay Ash across quote sites, and consistent with her message — but no book, speech, or date sources this exact wording. An honest "attributed."
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Don't limit yourself. Many people limit themselves to what they think they can do'?
meta.ogDescription: Uniformly credited to Mary Kay Ash and true to her voice — yet no primary source pins the wording. We mark it attributed, not verified.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.sourceLine: This line is credited to Mary Kay Ash almost everywhere it appears, and it fits her lifelong message of self-belief in business. But no quote database, biography, or archive ties the exact wording to a specific book, speech, or date — so it rests on attribution, not a located primary source.

source.heading: Where the line actually comes from

docMeta.dd: “… You can go as far as your mind lets you.”

source.excerpt: Don’t limit yourself. Many people limit themselves to what they think they can do. You can go as far as your mind lets you. What you believe, remember, you can achieve.
trail: The line is credited to Mary Kay Ash on virtually every quote aggregator — Goodreads carries the full four-sentence form but flags that its quotes are “added by the Goodreads community and are not verified.”
No primary source is attached anywhere: none of the databases name a book, page, speech, or date, and searches of her books turned up no located passage.
Neither Quote Investigator nor Wikiquote has an investigated or sourced entry for this line — Wikiquote has no Mary Kay Ash page at all — so there is no specialist anchor to lean on.

No rival originator surfaced: nobody else is credited with the wording, and it is fully consistent with Ash’s documented “you can do it” message, which is why we treat it as attributed rather than disputed.
source.excerptNote: The popular short version is the first two sentences; the fuller four-sentence form is what circulates on most quote sites. No edition, page, or speech date accompanies it anywhere we found.
source.rightsNote: Because the exact wording can’t be tied to a specific dated work, we assert no copyright status. If it does come from one of Mary Kay Ash’s books (all published between 1981 and 1995), that work would be in copyright — but since no source is located, the honest classification is uncertain.

author.name: Mary Kay Ash
author.heading: About Mary Kay Ash
author.metaLine: 1918–2001 · American businesswoman · Founder of Mary Kay Cosmetics
author.bio: Mary Kay Ash founded Mary Kay Cosmetics in 1963 and built it into one of the largest direct-sales companies in the world, championing a motivational, faith-and-praise management style aimed at women in business. She was famous for aphorisms about self-belief and unlimited potential, which is why lines like this one attach to her name so readily — and why they need checking.

cite.sourceCitation: Attributed to Mary Kay Ash; earliest documented appearances are undated entries on quote-aggregator sites (e.g. Goodreads, BrainyQuote). No primary book, speech, or interview source has been located.
cite.pageCitation: Quotle.info. “Who really said ‘Don't limit yourself. Many people limit themselves to what they think they can do’?” Last verified 16 Jul 2026.

misattribution.heading: A caution, not a debunking
misattribution.intro: There is no sign this line belongs to anyone but Mary Kay Ash. The issue is thinner than a wrong name: the wording travels with zero sourcing, so “verified” would overstate what anyone can actually show.

items.why: Goodreads, BrainyQuote, A-Z Quotes and Quotefancy all attach the line to Ash with no book, page, speech, or date — and Goodreads warns its quotes are community-added and unverified.
Neither has investigated or sourced this line; Wikiquote has no Mary Kay Ash page at all, so there is no authoritative confirmation to cite.

misattribution.truthLine: Best read as genuinely Mary Kay Ash in spirit and voice, but attributed, not verified — no one has yet pointed to the book, speech, or page where she first said it (Goodreads).

context.heading: Why it sounds like her
lead: Mary Kay Ash built a company — and a management philosophy — around telling saleswomen they could achieve far more than they believed. Lines about refusing to limit yourself are the core of that message, which is exactly why this one sits comfortably under her name.

That fit is also the trap. A sentiment perfectly on-brand for a motivational figure is the easiest kind of quote to attach to them without evidence, and this line has spread for years on aggregator sites that copy each other rather than a documented source.
context.pull: On-brand enough to sound certain — unsourced enough to stay honest about.
